**All experiments done. One paper wins: Procedural Pretraining.**

| Variant (paper) | Placement | Wiki PPL | BLiMP | ARC-E | Overall | Efficiency | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline 2B@10% (STM pipeline) | — | 4.861 | 58.81 | 34.40 | 59.59 | 9.90 (10/36) | reference |
| **Procedural warm-up** (2601.21725) | before training | 4.981 | **61.79** | 34.00 | **60.30** | **10.02 (7/36)** | **WIN +0.71** |
| Deep-and-thin (2402.14905) | architecture | 4.937 | 60.27 | 33.20 | 59.59 | 9.90 | tie — rejected |
| Output Emb. Centering (2601.02031) | during training | 5.109 | 57.76 | 31.60 | 58.01 | 9.64 (12/36) | **diverged — rejected** |
| proc_after | after first SLERP | 4.861 | 58.81 | 34.40 | 59.59 | 9.90 | lost tournament |
| oec_after | after first SLERP | 4.861 | 58.81 | 34.40 | 59.59 | 9.90 | lost tournament |

What the table says:
- **Procedural warm-up**: 5M Dyck tokens (0.25% of budget) front-loaded → +0.71 overall, BLiMP project record 61.79, efficiency rank 7/36. Paper's claim reproduced at 1M scale.
- **Before vs after SLERP**: same pattern as STM — both after-champion placements actively hurt the model (proc_after pushed wiki PPL to 5.273; oec_after dropped ARC to 31.8) and the tournament just re-picked the unmodified baseline merge. These techniques only pay front-loaded.
- **Deep-thin**: BLiMP up, wiki/ARC down, exact overall tie. Likely because the looped-shared-block already buys effective depth.
- **OEC**: NaN'd twice between steps 5600–10000. Root cause: μ-centering a **tied** embedding mutates the input embedding outside optimizer state each step. Side-finding logged: STM's `select_survivors` keeps everything under NaN losses (comparisons all False) — it ran 3 harmless no-op rounds on the corpse.

All six rows in scores.md, full journal entry, committed. Full test suite re-running in background now that the GPU is free. Open follow-ups (untested, say the word): wire procedural warm-up into `train.py` as default like STM; OEC retry with an untied output head; proc + deepthin combination.
